summary: Simplify the names of the fretboard modes
detail: Current seven: Roots, Chord positions, CAGED triads, CAGED arpeggios, Triad inversions, CAGED pentatonic, CAGED scales. Four start with "CAGED", and the row is 144px tall on a phone. Depends on the outcome of T4 and T5, which may cut the list first.
resolution: Done 2026-09-07. Six one-word names: Roots, Progression, Chords, Triads, Pentatonic, Scales. The tab is already called CAGED practice and the legend already says 'C shape', so the prefix carried nothing. Mode row on a phone: 144px before the T4 merge, 107px after it, 69px now. data-value attributes are unchanged, so no JS depended on the rename; comments, tooltips and the README follow the new names.

summary: Put a play/pause button back in the playback controls section
detail: T10 made the single Play button float, which took it out of the controls list where it used to sit. Add one back there as well, so the transport section reads complete, and keep the floating one. Both need to show the same play/pause state and label, so setPlayLabel() should drive a set of buttons rather than one element.
resolution: Done 2026-09-07. A second Play sits in the transport list; the floating one keeps its own class. setPlayLabel() and the click handler now drive every .play-btn, so both show the same state and either one toggles playback.

summary: CAGED chords single box: option to ghost the rest of the progression
detail: While practising one grip, show where the progression's other chords sit in that same position, drawn fainter, the way Chord positions dims everything but the sounding chord. Optional, via a toggle in the Shapes row. Can reuse what Chord positions already has: ROOT_PALETTE for per-chord colour and the pos-follow / pos-current / pos-next CSS tiers. Note CAGED chords is currently a single-chord view driven by the chord picker, so it would need the other chords' grips computed for the same fret window.
resolution: Done 2026-09-07. An 'Other chords' toggle in the Shapes row draws the progression's remaining chords into the current box, following the view in front (grips when shape-only, chord tones with Whole arpeggio) and skipping frets the chord in front already uses. Needs Single box on, since it fills one position. Drawn exactly the way Progression draws them during playback: each chord in its ROOT_PALETTE colour, labelled by degree with the root by name, its grip traced faintly, and everything that isn't the chord in front dimmed on Progression's own three playback tiers - the chord in front lit, the chord after it at 0.4 (outlines 0.3), the rest at 0.07 (outlines 0.04), roots included and with no anchor-root exception, since that is Progression's at-rest reading rather than its playback one. The next tier follows the chord picker and wraps at the end of the progression. Legend entries name each chord with its numeral in Progression's format. Ghosts are excluded from collectShapeRanges so they can't distort a shape's fret span.

summary: Re-order the practice tab: chart, fretboard, key/chord settings, playback settings
detail: Split the chord chart out of the playback-controls panel. New top-to-bottom order: (1) the chord chart on its own at the very top, (2) the fretboard, (3) the key and chord settings, (4) the playback settings. Also add a copy of the 60/90/120 BPM buttons beneath the floating play button, so tempo is reachable without scrolling to the playback settings. Supersedes the T1 arrangement, which put the transport above the chart within one panel.
resolution: Done 2026-09-07. The practice tab is now chart / fretboard / key-and-chord settings / playback settings, top to bottom, with the chart split out of the playback panel into one of its own. Play and a second copy of the 60/90/120 BPM buttons float together bottom-right in one cluster; both BPM sets and both Play buttons stay in sync with no JS change, since the handlers already bind over every .bpm-preset and .play-btn. Verified at 375/768/1280: chart-to-neck gap 66px, both fit one screen, no overflow, the cluster clears the last panel and never covers the chart.

summary: Chords mode: offer Progression's "voice leading" as an alternative to Single box
detail: In Chords mode, add voice leading alongside Single box as a way of choosing which grip to show: instead of stepping boxes by position, each chord takes the grip nearest where the previous one landed, the way Progression's Voice leading toggle already works. Builds on T14, which put the other chords in the same picture. When done, report on whether keeping both Progression and Chords as separate modes still makes sense.
resolution: Done 2026-09-07. A 'Voice leading' toggle in the Shapes row lets the progression choose the box instead of you: the first chord takes its lowest, each one after it takes whichever of its own boxes sits nearest where the last landed. On D-Em-Bm that gives 0-3 / 0-2 / 2-4 - the hand walking rather than jumping. It is deterministic (same chain whatever you were looking at before), works with Whole arpeggio and Other chords, and locks the box stepper and Single box while it is on. See the session report for the Progression-vs-Chords answer: keep both.

summary: Open on the first preset for the key's mode rather than a random progression
detail: practice.init() currently picks a random key and calls render(), which rolls random chords. Instead, land on the first entry of the preset list for whichever mode the key is in - the same list buildPresetSelect() builds - so a fresh page opens on a recognisable progression and the preset picker shows what is loaded. A shared link still wins over this.

summary: Quick actions in the chord chart panel: pick a key, pick a preset
detail: The chart now sits alone at the top while the key and preset pickers are two panels down. Put quick actions in the chart panel itself: one to choose a specific key or a random one, and one to choose a preset progression for whichever mode that key is in. They should drive the same state as the pickers in the settings panel, not a parallel copy.
